conflict_resolutions.EMPTY_CATALOG_NOTE_DOES_NOT_ESTABLISH_CU: The Federal Register catalog observation for Executive Order 13624 has an empty disposition note, which neither shows current effect nor an ending and is not used as a basis. I searched the held corpus for the order's number (only the order's own text and a Department of Energy notice signed January 5, 2026, FR Doc. 2026-00153, which cites the order as authority for an information collection and does not end it), read the three bounded machine searches (no hit that ends it), and read the order's own terms (continuing directions to agencies with no sunset or expiry). The status rests on those and on the United States Code note under 42 U.S.C. 6341 that prints the order in full with no ending statement.

notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: Executive Order 13624 (August 30, 2012; 77 FR 54779) directs the Departments of Energy, Commerce and Agriculture and the Environmental Protection Agency to coordinate policies encouraging investment in industrial energy efficiency and combined heat and power, to engage stakeholders, and to take the listed supporting actions. The held original has no sunset, expiry, termination condition or revocation; the end-of-2020 date in Sec. 2(a) is the target date of a national goal, not an end of the direction. No held later order, statute or regulation amends, revokes or supersedes it. The United States Code (release point 119-121, printed through 2026-10-09) prints the order in full as a note under 42 U.S.C. 6341 with no ending statement, and a Department of Energy Federal Register notice signed January 5, 2026 still cites it as authority. Coverage gap: laws enacted 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that release, and no held source suggests any touches the order. Recommended provisional status: yes.
